chunks: Yet the unbelievers say: 'This is nothing but a lie he has concocted in which others have aided him.' They have come down to mischief and lies.
ai.seo_question: What did the disbelievers claim about the origin of the Quran according to Surah Al-Furqan?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the 'sahaba' (companions) mentioned by the disbelievers, often interpreted as the scribes of revelation like Zayd ibn Thabit, whose assistance was viewed as proof of the Quran's human-like structure rather than divine origin. The characterization of their claim as 'zulman wa zuran' (injustice and falsehood) underscores the epistemological error of attributing divine speech to human collaboration, a theme central to the doctrine of I'jaz (inimitability).
